pick.headline: Czechoslovak communist leadership resigns
pick.summary: On November 24, 1989, after a week of mass demonstrations, Milos Jakes and the Czechoslovak Communist Party leadership resigned.
pick.significance: The resignation, a week after the student march was beaten, showed how fast the Velvet Revolution had broken the regime.
pick.fbis: Prague's domestic service reported on the night of November 24 that Milos Jakes had spoken at the emergency Central Committee session and that Karel Urbanek had been elected general secretary.
